To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
fasting increases fatty acid oxidation and decreases esterification in isolated rat liver cells.

the partition of palmitate between esterification to lipids and oxidation to ketone bodies in the liver is altered by the nutritional status and that this change in partitioning results from a decrease in the oxidation of nonfatty acid substrates in the fasting state and from an increase in the availability of long chain fatty acid in the fed state.

the partition of palmitate between esterification to glycerolipids and oxidation to ketone bodies is altered by the nutritional state of the animal and that the availability of nonfatty acid substrates is a major factor in the altered partition of free palmitic acid in the liver.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the metabolism and partitioning of free fatty acids and their derivatives in isolated liver cells and the effect of fasting on these processes.
the metabolism of free fatty acids by the isolated rat liver cell and the effect of fasting, palmitate concentration, and non-fatty acid substrate concentration on fatty acid utilization.
the partition of long chain fatty acid metabolism between oxidation and esterifications and the factors which influence this partition in the fasting and fed states.

the major factor responsible for the increased ketogenesis of fatty acids in liver cells in the fasting state is an increased partition between esterified and ketone body formation.

the partition of free fatty acid metabolism between oxidation and esterfication is regulated by a variety of mechanisms which include the availability of long chain fatty acid substrates, the availability of non-faty acid substrates which are oxidized in preference to fatty acids, the availability of glycerol for esterification of fatty acids, and the availability of long and short chain acyl CoA thioesters for β oxidation and ester formation, respectively.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the partition of free fatty acid metabolism in liver cells is determined by the relative rates of oxidation and esterifiction.
the partition of fatty acid oxidation and esterfication is a major factor in determining ketogenesis and that this partition is altered by the nutritional state of the animal.
fasting decreases the rate of esterification of fatty acids and decreases the partition between oxidation and esterfication.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the liver has a very important role in the regulation of fatty acid utilization.
the liver plays a key role in regulating the availability of fatty acids to the rest of the body.
we have demonstrated that fatty acid oxidation is a major determinant of the partition of long chain free acids between oxidation and esterfication in liver cells.
